newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open softer, underperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open softer, underperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Monday, underperforming U.S. Treasuries, with weakness in the Canadian dollar and concern about upcoming data weighing on prices, analysts said.

"It's not so much the story with Canada as internationally what came out of the G-7. Canada is just sort of selling off along with all the other currencies here. The U.S. dollar is strong against absolutely everything," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities. Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.42 to C$107.20 to yield 7.374 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 3/32 to yield 7.15 percent. The spread between the two bonds widened to 22 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

The Canadian dollar opened softer against the U.S. currency, which reached new 37-month high against the mark after investors interpreted a benign Group of Seven statement on exchange rates as a green light to buy the currency. The Canadian dollar's weakness came after Canada set an official election date of June 2. Traders said the election is unlikely to have a dramatic near-term impact on financial markets because the ruling Liberal Party is a clear front-runner.

Canadian and U.S. bonds are now looking ahead to this week's key U.S. employment cost, gross domestic product and payroll employment data. The reports are seen as a key indication of whether U.S. interest rates will rise further.

"We think the market is set up technically to weaken unless the data is a big surprise here, so I don't think bad numbers so to speak are fully priced in by any means. I think we can weaken further," said Webber. "If those numbers reinforce the idea that the Fed is going to be moving on May 20 that in turn is negative for the Canadian dollar and will be negative for Canadian bonds."
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.35 to C$100.95 to yield 6.862 percent. The U.S. bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.95 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to nine basis points from 12 basis points on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.19 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.34 percent.
